verses.zh: 但愿你们宽容我这一点愚妄，其实你们原是宽容我的。
verses.en: I wish that you would be patient with me in a little foolishness, but indeed you are being patient with me!

verses.zh: 我为你们起的愤恨，原是　神那样的愤恨。因为我曾把你们许配一个丈夫，要把你们如同贞洁的童女，献给基督。
verses.en: For I am jealous for you with godly jealousy, because I promised you in marriage to one husband,[NOTE:1] to present you as a pure[NOTE:2] virgin to Christ.
notes: That is, to Christ.
Or “chaste.”

verses.zh: 我只怕你们的心或偏于邪，失去那向基督所存纯一清洁的心，就像蛇用诡诈诱惑了夏娃一样。
verses.en: But I am afraid that[NOTE:1] just as the serpent[NOTE:2] deceived Eve by his treachery,[NOTE:3] your minds may be led astray[NOTE:4] from a sincere and pure[NOTE:5] devotion to Christ.
notes: Grk “I fear lest somehow.”
Or “the snake.”
Or “craftiness.”
Or “corrupted,” “seduced.”

Although most mss (א2 H Ψ 0121 0243 1739 1881 M) lack “and pure” (καὶ τῆς ἁγνότητος, kai tēs hagnotētos; Grk “and purity”) several significant and early witnesses (P46 א* B D[2] F G 33 81 104 ar r co) retain these words. Their presence in such mss across such a wide geographical distribution argues for their authenticity. The omission from the majority of mss can be explained by haplography, since the -τητος ending of ἁγνότητος is identical to the ending of ἁπλότητος (haplotētos, “sincerity”) three words back (ἁπλότητος καὶ τῆς ἁγνότητος); further, since the meanings of “sincerity” and “purity” are similar they might seem redundant. A copyist would scarcely notice the omission because Paul’s statement still makes sense without “and from purity.”

verses.zh: 假如有人来另传一个耶稣，不是我们所传过的；或者你们另受一个灵，不是你们所受过的；或者另得一个福音，不是你们所得过的；你们容让他也就罢了。
verses.en: For if someone comes and proclaims[NOTE:1] another Jesus different from the one we proclaimed,[NOTE:2] or if you receive a different spirit than the one you received,[NOTE:3] or a different gospel than the one you accepted,[NOTE:4] you put up with it well enough![NOTE:5]
notes: Or “preaches.”
Grk “another Jesus whom we have not proclaimed.”
Grk “a different spirit which you did not receive.”
Grk “a different gospel which you did not accept.”
Or “you endure it very well.”

verses.zh: 但我想，我一点不在那些最大的使徒以下。
verses.en: For I consider myself not at all inferior to those “super-apostles.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The implicit irony in Paul’s remark is brought out well by the TEV “I do not think that I am the least bit inferior to those very special so-called ‘apostles’ of yours!”sn The ‘super-apostles’ refers either (1) to the original apostles (the older interpretation) or (2) more probably, to Paul’s opponents in Corinth, in which case the designation is ironic.

verses.zh: 我的言语虽然粗俗，我的知识却不粗俗。这是我们在凡事上向你们众人显明出来的。
verses.en: And even if I am unskilled[NOTE:1] in speaking, yet I am certainly not so in knowledge. Indeed, we have made this plain to you in everything in every way.
notes: Unskilled in speaking means not professionally trained as a rhetorician.

verses.zh: 我因为白白传　神的福音给你们，就自居卑微，叫你们高升，这算是我犯罪吗？
verses.en: Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself[NOTE:1] so that you could be exalted, because I proclaimed[NOTE:2] the gospel of God to you free of charge?
notes: Paul is referring to humbling himself to the point of doing manual labor to support himself.
Or “preached.”

verses.zh: 我亏负了别的教会，向他们取了工价来给你们效力。
verses.en: I robbed other churches by receiving support from them so that I could serve you![NOTE:1]
notes: That is, serve them free of charge (cf. the end of v. 7).

verses.zh: 我在你们那里缺乏的时候，并没有累着你们一个人；因我所缺乏的，那从马其顿来的弟兄们都补足了。我向来凡事谨守，后来也必谨守，总不至于累着你们。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] I was with you and was in need, I was not a burden to anyone, for the brothers who came from Macedonia fully supplied my needs.[NOTE:2] I[NOTE:3] kept myself from being a burden to you in any way, and will continue to do so.
notes: Grk “you, and when.” A new sentence was started here in the translation.

If the participle ἐλθόντες (elthontes) is taken as temporal rather than adjectival, the translation would be, “for the brothers, when they came from Macedonia, fully supplied my needs” (similar to NASB).
Grk “needs, and I kept.” A new sentence was started here in the translation.

verses.zh: 既有基督的诚实在我里面，就无人能在亚该亚一带地方阻挡我这自夸。
verses.en: As the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine[NOTE:1] will not be stopped[NOTE:2] in the regions of Achaia.
notes: That is, that Paul offers the gospel free of charge to the Corinthians (see 2 Cor 11:7).
Or “silenced.”

verses.zh: 为甚么呢？是因我不爱你们吗？这有　神知道。
verses.en: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do![NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “God knows!” The words “I do” are supplied for clarity. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context.

verses.zh: 我现在所做的，后来还要做，为要断绝那些寻机会人的机会，使他们在所夸的事上也不过与我们一样。
verses.en: And what I am doing I will continue to do, so that I may eliminate any opportunity for those who want a chance to be regarded as our equals[NOTE:1] in the things they boast about.
notes: Grk “an opportunity, so that they may be found just like us.”

verses.zh: 那等人是假使徒，行事诡诈，装作基督使徒的模样。
verses.en: For such people are false apostles, deceitful[NOTE:1] workers, disguising themselves[NOTE:2] as apostles of Christ.
notes: Or “dishonest.”
Or “workers, masquerading.”

verses.zh: 这也不足为怪，因为连撒但也装作光明的天使。
verses.en: And no wonder, for even Satan disguises himself[NOTE:1] as an angel of light.
notes: Or “Satan himself masquerades.”

verses.zh: 所以他的差役，若装作仁义的差役，也不算希奇。他们的结局必然照着他们的行为。
verses.en: Therefore it is not surprising his servants also disguise themselves[NOTE:1] as servants of righteousness, whose end will correspond to their actions.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “also masquerade.”
Or “their works.”

verses.zh: 我再说，人不可把我看作愚妄的。纵然如此，也要把我当作愚妄人接纳，叫我可以略略自夸。
verses.en: I say again, let no one think that I am a fool.[NOTE:1] But if you do, then at least accept me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
notes: Or “am foolish.”

verses.zh: 我说的话不是奉主命说的，乃是像愚妄人放胆自夸；
verses.en: What I am saying with this boastful confidence[NOTE:1] I do not say the way the Lord would.[NOTE:2] Instead it is, as it were, foolishness.
notes: Grk “with this confidence of boasting.” The genitive καυχήσεως (kauchēseōs) has been translated as an attributive genitive (the noun in the genitive functions as an adjective of the noun modified).
Or “say with the Lord’s authority.”

verses.zh: 既有好些人凭着血气自夸，我也要自夸了。
verses.en: Since many[NOTE:1] are boasting according to human standards,[NOTE:2] I too will boast.
notes: Many is a reference to Paul’s opponents.
Grk “according to the flesh.”

verses.zh: 你们既是精明人，就能甘心忍耐愚妄人。
verses.en: For since you are so wise, you put up with[NOTE:1] fools gladly.
notes: Or “you tolerate.”

verses.zh: 假若有人强你们作奴仆，或侵吞你们，或掳掠你们，或侮慢你们，或打你们的脸，你们都能忍耐他。
verses.en: For you put up with[NOTE:1] it if someone makes slaves of you, if someone exploits you, if someone takes advantage of you, if someone behaves arrogantly[NOTE:2] toward you, if someone strikes you in the face.
notes: Or “you tolerate.”

verses.zh: 我说这话是羞辱自己，好像我们从前是软弱的。然而，人在何事上勇敢，（我说句愚妄话，）我也勇敢。
verses.en: (To my disgrace[NOTE:1] I must say that we were too weak for that!)[NOTE:2] But whatever anyone else dares to boast about[NOTE:3] (I am speaking foolishly), I also dare to boast about the same thing.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “my shame.”

It seems best, in context, to see the statement we were too weak for that as a parenthetical and ironic comment by Paul on his physical condition (weakness or sickness) while he was with the Corinthians (cf. 2 Cor 12:7-10; Gal 4:15).

The words “to boast about” are not in the Greek text, but are implied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context, and this phrase serves as the direct object of the preceding verb.

Grk “I also dare”; the words “to boast about the same thing” are not in the Greek text, but are implied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context, and this phrase serves as the direct object of the preceding verb.

verses.zh: 他们是希伯来人吗？我也是。他们是以色列人吗？我也是。他们是亚伯拉罕的后裔吗？我也是。
verses.en: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.

verses.zh: 他们是基督的仆人吗？（我说句狂话，）我更是。我比他们多受劳苦，多下监牢，受鞭打是过重的，冒死是屡次有的。
verses.en: Are they servants of Christ? (I am talking like I am out of my mind!) I am even more so: with much greater labors, with far more imprisonments, with more severe beatings, facing death many times.

verses.zh: 被犹太人鞭打五次，每次四十减去一下；
verses.en: Five times I received from the Jews forty lashes less one.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “forty less one”; this was a standard sentence. “Lashes” is supplied to clarify for the modern reader what is meant.

verses.zh: 被棍打了三次；被石头打了一次；遇着船坏三次，一昼一夜在深海里。
verses.en: Three times I was beaten with a rod.[NOTE:1] Once I received a stoning.[NOTE:2] Three times I suffered shipwreck. A night and a day I spent adrift in the open sea.
notes: Beaten with a rod refers to the Roman punishment of admonitio according to BDAG 902 s.v. ῥαβδίζω. Acts 16:22 describes one of these occasions in Philippi; in this case it was administered by the city magistrates, who had wide powers in a military colony.
Received a stoning. See Acts 14:19, where this incident is described.

verses.zh: 又屡次行远路，遭江河的危险、盗贼的危险、同族的危险、外邦人的危险、城里的危险、旷野的危险、海中的危险、假弟兄的危险。
verses.en: I have been on journeys many times, in dangers from rivers, in dangers from robbers,[NOTE:1] in dangers from my own countrymen, in dangers from Gentiles, in dangers in the city, in dangers in the wilderness,[NOTE:2] in dangers at sea, in dangers from false brothers,
notes: Or “bandits.” The word normally refers more to highwaymen (“robbers”) but can also refer to insurrectionists or revolutionaries (“bandits”).
Or “desert.”

verses.zh: 受劳碌、受困苦，多次不得睡，又饥又渴，多次不得食，受寒冷，赤身露体。
verses.en: in hard work and toil,[NOTE:1] through many sleepless nights, in hunger and thirst, many times without food, in cold and without enough clothing.[NOTE:2]
notes: The two different words for labor are translated “in hard work and toil” by L&N 42.48.

Grk “in cold and nakedness.” Paul does not mean complete nakedness, however, which would have been repugnant to a Jew; he refers instead to the lack of sufficient clothing, especially in cold weather. A related word is used to 1 Cor 4:11, also in combination with experiencing hunger and thirst.

verses.zh: 除了这外面的事，还有为众教会挂心的事，天天压在我身上。
verses.en: Apart from other things,[NOTE:1] there is the daily pressure on me of my anxious concern[NOTE:2] for all the churches.
notes: Apart from other things. Paul refers here either (1) to the external sufferings just mentioned, or (2) he refers to other things he has left unmentioned.
“Anxious concern,” so translated in L&N 25.224.

verses.zh: 有谁软弱，我不软弱呢？有谁跌倒，我不焦急呢？
verses.en: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin,[NOTE:1] and I do not burn with indignation?
notes: Or “who is caused to stumble.”

verses.zh: 我若必须自夸，就夸那关乎我软弱的事便了。
verses.en: If I must boast,[NOTE:1] I will boast about the things that show my weakness.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “If boasting is necessary.”
Or “about the things related to my weakness.”

verses.zh: 那永远可称颂之主耶稣的父　神知道我不说谎。
verses.en: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is blessed forever, knows I am not lying.

verses.zh: 在大马士革的亚哩达王手下的提督把守大马士革城，要捉拿我，
verses.en: In Damascus, the governor[NOTE:1] under King Aretas was guarding the city of Damascus[NOTE:2] in order to arrest[NOTE:3] me,
notes: Grk “ethnarch.”sn The governor was an official called an “ethnarch” who was appointed to rule on behalf of a king over a certain region.
Grk “the city of the Damascenes.”
Or “to seize,” “to catch.”

verses.zh: 我就从窗户中，在筐子里，从城墙上被人缒下去，脱离了他的手。
verses.en: but I was let down in a rope-basket[NOTE:1] through a window in the city wall, and escaped his hands.
notes: In Acts 9:25 the same basket used in Paul’s escape is called a σπυρίς (spuris), a basket larger than a κόφινος (kophinos). It was very likely made out of rope, so the translation “rope-basket” is used.
